messages:
customer_jason: Hey team, seeing frequent streaming responses cut off mid-event. Client logs show "write failed: Broken pipe" followed by curl exit. Billing is reporting these as 5xx for our account (acme-inc). Sample request ids: req_A1B2C3, req_D4E5F6. Region: us-west2.

customer_jason: Repro we ran (we're going through an on-prem nginx 1.18 reverse proxy):
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  --no-buffer \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-x","input":"long streaming test..."}'
```

support_eng: Thanks. Can you paste the nginx error logs and the gateway response headers? Also confirm whether nginx is terminating HTTP/2 to upstream or proxying HTTP/1.1.

customer_jason: nginx error snippet: 
```
2026/03/11 09:12:05 [error] 1187#0: *4521 writev() failed (32: Broken pipe) while sending to client, client: 10.10.10.5, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://10.20.30.40:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai"
```
We reproduce locally by running same nginx in front of our curl/SDK. Failure rate increases for responses > ~8k tokens.

oncall_sre: tagging ingress-bot and eng-runtime. Sounds like a half-close race where client/proxy closes TCP while the gateway is flushing final chunk(s). Our current gateway logic increments 5xx when write fails during response flush, which likely conflates client aborts with internal errors.

ingress-bot: trace recorded: trace/4728912345 (spans: gw_span_aa -> svc_span_bb). Link: https://internal-traces/redwood/4728912345

support_eng: Diagnostic checklist:
- Try forcing HTTP/1.1 (curl --http1.1) to see if http2 multiplexing is exposing the race.
- Add header "Connection: keep-alive" and increase client timeouts.
- Disable response buffering in nginx (proxy_request_buffering off) to avoid extra buffering semantics.
- Reproduce with --no-buffer and verbose logs so timing isn't hidden.

customer_jason: Confirmed: forcing --http1.1 increases reproducibility of the cutoff for us (http/2 was more intermittent). Turning off response buffering reduced but did not eliminate occurrences.

oncall_sre: Plan of action:
1) Change gateway classification: if final chunk has been successfully queued/flushed and subsequent socket errors are EPIPE/ECONNRESET, mark as client_disconnect rather than 5xx.
2) Emit a new metric stream.client_disconnect with tags (customer, route, region) to separate billing signals.
3) Short-term recommend nginx config tweaks: proxy_request_buffering off; set proxy_read_timeout and keepalive_timeout to >=120s; prefer HTTP/1.1 to upstream where possible.

billing_team: If we reclassify these as client disconnects, we need the list of affected invoice_ids and per-request token counts so we can hold charges and reconcile. For acme-inc, please DM the request IDs.

support_eng: I'll pull the last 72h of request ids and estimated tokens and send to billing. We'll also tag the log entries with client_disconnect=true once SRE ships the change.

evan: Working on a patch. Approach: add an "end_of_stream_sent" flag in the gateway response path; if that flag is true and the next write or read returns EPIPE/ECONNRESET, classify as client_abort and don't increment 5xx metrics. Adding unit tests for half-close race and doing a staged rollout. ETA for patch to staging ~2 hours.

customer_jason: Appreciate the quick response. Any immediate mitigations we should apply in nginx?

support_eng: Temporary mitigations that helped other customers:
- proxy_request_buffering off;
- proxy_http_version 1.1;
- set proxy_set_header Connection "" (or keep-alive depending on flow);
- increase proxy_read_timeout and keepalive_timeout to 2-3 minutes;
These reduce the window for the half-close timing issue.

customer_jason: We'll apply the nginx changes and test. Thanks.

oncall_sre: Pushing the classification change to staging now and will enable the new metric. Once we get clean signals from canary, we'll update billing to ignore flagged client_disconnects for reconciliation. Will post status here after prod canary.

billing_team: Copy. Waiting on the request id list; will hold charges for affected timeframe for acme-inc until SRE confirms root cause and reclassification.

support_eng: Following up: I collected ~1200 candidate request ids for acme-inc from the last 72 hours (sample attached in DM). After canary, we'll annotate and let billing finalize. Next update in ~3 hours.

customer_jason: Thanks everyone, looking forward to the canary results. I will update this thread if the nginx change removes the failures on our side. :thumbsup:
